title: Land Dispute Mediation at Commune People's Committee: Mandatory?
desc: Land disputes must be mediated at the commune or ward People's Committee first: mediation council, 30-day limit, and when to go to court (Land Law 2024).
summary: The mandatory mediation procedure at the commune-level People's Committee for land disputes under Article 235 of the Land Law 2024, the 30-day period, and where to go next if mediation fails.
body: p

Disputes over boundaries, access paths, and inherited land between neighbors or siblings are common before building a house. The Land Law 2024 encourages the parties to mediate themselves and provides for mandatory mediation at the commune-level People's Committee before a competent authority resolves the dispute (Article 235 of the Land Law).
h2
1. Is mediation at the commune People's Committee mandatory?
p

Yes. Under Clause 2, Article 235, before a competent state authority resolves a land dispute under Article 236 (including the Court and the People's Committee), the disputing parties must mediate at the commune-level People's Committee where the land is located. In addition, the parties may still mediate among themselves, use community-level mediation (village or residential group), or use commercial mediation (Clause 1).
h2
2. Who sits on the Mediation Council?
p
After receiving a request for mediation, the Chairperson of the commune-level People's Committee establishes a Land Dispute Mediation Council, consisting of:
ul
The Chairperson or a Vice Chairperson of the commune-level People's Committee, as Chair of the Council;
A representative of the commune-level Vietnam Fatherland Front Committee;
The land administration (cadastral) official;
A long-time resident who knows the origin and history of use of the plot (if any);
Other organizations and individuals may be invited as appropriate.
h2
3. Mediation period and outcome
ul
Mediation at the commune-level People's Committee is carried out within no more than 30 days from receipt of the request (Point c, Clause 2, Article 235).

A record must be prepared, signed by the parties, with confirmation by the commune-level People's Committee that mediation succeeded or failed; the record is sent to the parties and kept at the commune People's Committee.
If mediation fails and a party does not sign: the Chair of the Council and the members sign, the commune People's Committee seal is applied, and the record is sent to the parties.

If mediation succeeds and changes the boundary, area, or land user: within 30 working days of receiving the document recognizing the result, the parties send a document to the competent authority to register and issue a Certificate (Clause 4, Article 235).
h2
4. If mediation fails, where is the dispute resolved?
p
Under Article 236 of the Land Law:
ul

If one of the parties holds a Certificate (land use right certificate, sổ đỏ) or documents on land use rights under Article 137, or the dispute concerns assets attached to the land: the Court resolves it.
If the parties have no Certificate or documents: they may choose to file with the competent-level People's Committee or to sue in Court under civil procedure law.
Disputes arising from commercial activities related to land are resolved by the Court or by Arbitration.
h2
5. What to prepare for mediation
ol
A request for mediation sent to the commune or ward People's Committee where the land is located, stating clearly the disputed part of the land.
Copies of the Certificate, land documents, maps, and cadastral extracts (if any).
Documents proving the history of use: tax receipts, sale contracts, wills, and so on.
A list of witnesses who know the origin of the land well.
p

While a dispute exists, the plot cannot be issued a land use right certificate (sổ đỏ) (Point e, Clause 1, Article 151) and cannot be transferred (Point b, Clause 1, Article 45). The undisputed part, if its boundary can be determined, can still be subdivided (Point c, Clause 1, Article 220).
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. Article 236 of the Land Law 2024 still names the authority of the Chairperson of the district-level People's Committee; after the abolition of the district level (two-level local government), this authority has been reassigned by documents not yet in our library; it is advisable to ask the commune- or ward-level People's Committee or a lawyer before filing.
